chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Muskān, from Abu Abdullah (the slave of Abd Rabbih), from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the mineral that comes out of the mine, in which there is gold, silver, and copper all together. How should we buy it? He said, 'Buy it with gold and silver all together.'
ai.seo_question: How to buy mixed gold and silver ore according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific case of purchasing raw ore containing gold, silver, and copper, ruling that it must be bought using a combination of gold and silver currencies. This ensures the preservation of value across all constituent precious metals, preventing the undervaluation of any single component during the exchange. The ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on precise valuation (*thaman*) in commodity trades to avoid *riba* (usury) and ensure equitable trade practices.
